quick: Data insufficient; use only if clearly needed
Avoid; no benefit and added CNS effects
summary: Atomoxetine is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (non-stimulant) for ADHD in children, adolescents and adults. It carries a BOXED WARNING for increased suicidal ideation in children and adolescents. Pediatric dosing is weight-based (start 0.5 mg/kg, target 1.2 mg/kg, max 1.4 mg/kg or 100 mg); adults and children over 70 kg start 40 mg, target 80 mg (max 100 mg). Reduce the dose in hepatic impairment and with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors / poor metabolizers. Key risks: suicidality, severe liver injury and cardiovascular effects.
indications: Treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in pediatric and adult patients

dosage.d: Start ~0.5 mg/kg/day; after >=3 days increase to target ~1.2 mg/kg/day
dosage.t: Once daily or divided AM + late afternoon
dosage.n: Max 1.4 mg/kg or 100 mg/day, whichever is less

dosage.d: Start 40 mg/day; after >=3 days increase to target 80 mg/day
dosage.n: May increase to max 100 mg/day after 2-4 weeks if needed

dosage.d: Reduce initial and target doses to 50% of normal
Reduce initial and target doses to 25% of normal
Start low and increase to usual target only if tolerated after ~4 weeks

admin: May be taken with or without food; given as a single morning dose or divided (morning and late afternoon/early evening)
Do not open capsules - contents are an ocular irritant; swallow whole
Do not start within 2 weeks of an MAOI
Titrate only after a minimum of 3 days at the starting dose
Monitor closely for suicidality, especially early in treatment and after dose changes
moa: The precise mechanism in ADHD is unknown but is thought to relate to selective inhibition of the presynaptic norepinephrine transporter, increasing synaptic norepinephrine. Unlike stimulants, it is not a controlled substance and has low abuse potential.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to atomoxetine or product components
Use with an MAOI or within 2 weeks of stopping an MAOI
Severe cardiovascular disorders that would deteriorate with increases in heart rate or blood pressure
relative: History of psychosis, bipolar disorder or aggression

preg: Available human data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk; some animal studies showed adverse developmental effects. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. A pregnancy exposure registry exists for ADHD medications.
lact: Limited data on excretion into human milk. Use with caution and weigh the benefit of treatment against potential risk to the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed. Although systemic exposure is higher in end-stage renal disease, there is no difference when corrected for mg/kg dose.
hepatic: Reduce the dose for hepatic impairment: to 50% of normal in moderate (Child-Pugh B) and 25% in severe (Child-Pugh C), owing to 2- to 4-fold increases in exposure. Discontinue and do not restart if jaundice or laboratory evidence of liver injury occurs.

major: MAOIs - contraindicated; risk of serious, sometimes fatal reactions (hyperthermia, autonomic instability) - separate by 2 weeks
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, quinidine) - markedly raise atomoxetine levels; reduce/titrate dose
moderate: Pressor agents / sympathomimetics - additive effects on blood pressure and heart rate
Albuterol and other beta-agonists - potentiated cardiovascular effects
minor: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold - theoretical additive risk
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; no therapeutic benefit and potential additive CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase heart rate and blood pressure; monitor liver enzymes if hepatotoxicity suspected.

serious: Serious cardiovascular events (sudden death, stroke, MI)
Marked increases in blood pressure/heart rate
Psychotic or manic symptoms; aggressive behavior
rare: Allergic reactions including angioedema and urticaria
emergency: Signs of liver injury (jaundice, dark urine, right-upper-quadrant pain)
Chest pain, syncope or signs of stroke/heart attack

monitoring: Suicidality, clinical worsening and unusual behavior changes - especially early and after dose changes
Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline and periodically
Liver function if symptoms of hepatic injury
Height and weight (growth) in children and adolescents
counsel: BOXED WARNING: watch for new or worsening depression, agitation or suicidal thoughts - especially in children/teens early in treatment - and contact the prescriber promptly
Stop the drug and seek care if jaundice, dark urine or right-sided abdominal pain occur (liver injury)
Do not open the capsule; it can irritate the eyes - wash eyes/hands if contents contact them
Full benefit may take several weeks; do not stop abruptly without advice
Report fainting, chest pain, palpitations or a prolonged erection immediately
pearls: BOXED WARNING: increased suicidal ideation in children and adolescents - monitor closely early in treatment
Non-stimulant, not a controlled substance - useful when stimulants are unsuitable or misuse is a concern
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and patients on strong CYP2D6 inhibitors need lower doses (higher exposure, longer half-life)
Reduce dose in hepatic impairment; discontinue for any sign of liver injury and do not rechallenge
Effect builds over weeks - set expectations for a gradual response
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is close to the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule - do not double the dose. The total daily dose should not exceed the recommended maximum.
overdose: Most overdoses cause somnolence, agitation, hyperactivity, GI symptoms, tachycardia and raised blood pressure; seizures and QT prolongation can occur. No specific antidote. Manage with airway/cardiac monitoring, supportive care and activated charcoal; high protein binding makes dialysis unlikely to help.
